S01: Before gods and before men, fate wove a thread for one child.
S02: Zeus: "You shall become the most legendary hero the world has ever seen."
S03: But not all of Olympus rejoiced.
S04: In the night, Hera sent two uninvited guests into the child's cradle.
S05: But the little child had wondrous strength.
S06: Thus began the tale of the hero whose name would be spoken for centuries.
S07: The years flew, and the boy grew into a powerful young man.
S08: Hercules: "I shall serve the king, however hard the task."
S09: Eurystheus: "Bring me the hide of the Nemean lion as proof!"
S10: The road to Nemea led through wild rocky lands.
S11: Before the cave awaited him a beast whose hide no arrow could pierce.
S12: Hercules met it with bare hands.
S13: When the arrows could not pierce it, only strength remained.
S14: The lion's hide became his sign and protection.
S15: The second task led to the swamp of Lerna, where a nine-headed monster dwelled.
S16: The Hydra had nine heads and sharp fangs.
S17: Every severed head gave birth to two new ones.
S19: With fire he stopped the regrowth and conquered the monster.
S20: From the blood of the Hydra, his arrows became a deadly weapon.
S21: The third task was a thieving hunt: a hind with golden antlers.
S22: Not with strength, but with patience.
S23: Hercules: "You are at peace now, O unreachable king."
S24: Then came an enormous boar on Mount Erymanthos.
S25: The people were afraid, but Hercules was not.
S26: When the boar was tamed, the return to the palace was triumphant.
S27: Then Eurystheus devised something seemingly impossible.
S28: Eurystheus: "Only a god can clean them!"
S29: Hercules: "And a hero can do it too!"
S30: He diverted the rivers and the water did the work.
S31: The stables gleamed clean, and Augeas was left without words.
S32: The fifth task led to Lake Stymphalia, full of terrible birds.
S33: Athena: "Take this rattle and shake it — it will frighten them!"
S34: The sound frightened the birds, and the arrows finished the work.
S35: One by one, the birds fell, and the lake became still.
S36: Eurystheus: "Athena got you out of a hard spot."
S37: Then, on Crete, a wild bull awaited him.
S38: With bare hands he tamed the wild bull.
S39: Eurystheus: "Bring me the girdle of their queen!"
S40: The Amazons were warriors and riders without equal.
S41: Hippolyta: "You are strong, but the girdle is earned with honor."
S42: With honor, not with cunning, he won the task.
S43: The tasks piled up, and his name grew.
S44: The hardest feats remained — the cattle of Geryon.
S45: With fire and with patience, he led the red herds home.
S46: Then — the golden apples at the western edge of the world.
S47: At the end awaited him the gate of the Underworld.
S48: There, the three-headed Cerberus guarded the threshold.
S49: With hands, not with sword, he tamed the last guardian too.
S51: The world spoke of him with reverence, and the gods watched.
S52: And among the stars was written the name of Hercules.
